newsitem.title: GERMANY: DASA stands behind Airbus large plane project.
newsitem.headline: DASA stands behind Airbus large plane project.

text.p: Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA), one of the principal partners in the Airbus consortium, said it fully backed the European plane maker's plans to continue developing a super-jumbo aircraft.

Airbus' U.S. rival Boeing Corp cast doubt on whether it would be possible to build a jet larger than its own 747 on Monday, saying it was scaling back work on developing its own version of the super jumbo, the 747-X.
But a DASA spokesman said there is still ample market demand for one of the jets, adding that Boeing's decision to pull out of the development race eased pressure on its own A3XX super jumbo project.
"Of course we are continuing with the A3XX project," a DASA spokesman said. "But we are not now under direct time pressure."
The spokesman said there appeared little chance that Seattle-based Boeing and Airbus would cooperate on developing one of the huge airliners.
The reason for the groups' different strategies is that they have different expectations about the future demand for large jetliners.

Airbus forecasts a market of 1,383 planes seating more than 400 passengers over the next 20 years, while Boeing believes demand would only stretch to 470 planes seating 500 or more, which would not allow it to get a return on its money.
DASA is the aerospace division of German industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG.
